title: ForgeFlow post-v2 operational hardening
objective: Eliminate the remaining operational ambiguity around runtime-unit drift and stale worktree state without expanding ForgeFlow runtime ownership.
architecture_decisions: ForgeFlow remains a thin quality-policy layer over Open SWE and LangGraph.
Runtime health inspection is read-only and must not silently activate or deactivate project supervision.
Git worktree cleanup is repository maintenance rather than ForgeFlow execution-state ownership.
ForgeFlow does not opt itself into continuous supervision unless an operator explicitly chooses that execution mode.
protected_contracts: Exact-head CI and independent review remain mandatory before READY.
Open SWE owns implementation and reviewer execution plus sandbox and workspace lifecycle.
No operational health output may expose secrets.
Existing systemd user-unit names and timer cadences remain stable.
non_goals: Do not resume another project's autonomous execution.
Do not redesign model routing, reviewer policy, TaskGraph scheduling, or provider fallback.
Do not add automatic deletion of arbitrary worktrees or remote branches.
acceptance_criteria: Required ForgeFlow user-unit inactivity is detected deterministically by a reusable read-only health check.
Installation asserts the required runtime units are active after enabling them.
Repository documentation defines evidence-based active-work and safe worktree-closure rules.
Focused deployment and documentation checks, Ruff, the full pytest suite, and git diff --check pass.

tasks.title: Make deployed runtime-unit health observable
tasks.goal: Add a deterministic read-only health check for required ForgeFlow user services and timers and enforce that postcondition at the end of installation.
tasks.why_now: The project-supervisor timer was observed enabled but inactive while the policy service remained healthy, and the current deployment surface does not expose that lifecycle drift as a reusable acceptance check.
scope: GCP Dev deployment and runtime health tooling under deploy/gcp-dev.
Installer postcondition after user timers are enabled.
out_of_scope: Automatically starting or stopping project supervision outside installation.
Changing timer cadence or project scheduling semantics.
Adding a second control plane or runtime state store.
protected_contracts: Health inspection is read-only and prints no secret values.
Existing unit names and deployment ownership remain unchanged.
implementation_steps: Characterize the required deployed user units and the enabled-but-inactive failure case with focused tests.
Implement the smallest reusable read-only runtime-unit health checker using systemd user-unit state.
Invoke the checker as an installer postcondition after required timers are enabled.
Cover healthy and inactive-unit behavior without making tests depend on the host systemd instance.
Update deployment documentation only where needed to describe the new acceptance surface.
integration_notes: The checker reports lifecycle drift but does not become an execution scheduler.
Project-level continuous_supervisor configuration remains independent from user-unit health.
acceptance_criteria: A required inactive unit or timer produces non-zero status and identifies the failed unit.
All required active units produce success.
Installer tests prove the postcondition is invoked after timer enablement.
Focused deployment tests, Ruff, full pytest, and git diff --check pass.
verification_commands: uv run ruff check deploy/gcp-dev tests/test_deployment.py tests/test_deploy_contract.py

tasks.title: Define active-work and worktree closure contract
tasks.goal: Document how operators distinguish active implementation state from stale worktrees and the evidence required before cleanup.
tasks.why_now: A large number of clean historical worktrees made completed September work look active even though no LangGraph runs or implementation processes were running.
scope: Documentation links needed to make the closure contract discoverable.
Documentation characterization tests if the repository uses them for required references.
out_of_scope: Changing Open SWE sandbox or workspace ownership.
protected_contracts: TaskGraph remains planning truth and LangGraph threads remain execution truth.
Open SWE retains sandbox and workspace lifecycle ownership.
No cleanup instruction may discard dirty work or an active process workspace.
implementation_steps: Add a concise operations runbook defining active plan, active TaskGraph, runtime thread and run, PR, and worktree evidence separately.
Define safe worktree-removal checks: clean status, no live process cwd, and merged, closed, or superseded delivery evidence.
Document that worktree count is not a proxy for active task count.
Document that ForgeFlow self-supervision remains opt-in rather than implied by an active plan.
Link the runbook from the appropriate documentation index and verify documentation checks.
integration_notes: The runbook describes maintenance boundaries; it does not grant ForgeFlow new worktree ownership.
This task can execute independently from FF-OPS-1001 because it owns only documentation.
acceptance_criteria: The active-work model distinguishes planning, execution, delivery, and filesystem evidence.
Safe cleanup requires clean, no-process, and delivery-closed evidence.
Documentation tests, full pytest, and git diff --check pass.
